title: Conjunctions and connecting words
subtitle: and, but, because, so, if, also, too
summary: Join two parts of a sentence with and, but, because, so and if, and connect ideas with only, like, than, also, too and as well.

lesson.heading: What conjunctions do
lesson.text: **Conjunctions** join two parts of a sentence. They show the connection between the two parts, so the listener knows if the second part is extra information, a contrast, a reason or a result.

examples.text: Kate is a student **and** she works part-time.
They are rich **but** they aren't happy.
You can pay by credit card **or** cash.

lesson.heading: Basic conjunctions
rows: Kate is a student and she works part-time.
They are rich but they aren't happy.
You can pay by credit card or cash.
We went home early because we were tired.
I felt ill so I didn't go to work.

lesson.heading: Time conjunctions and if
rows: I went to the party when the babysitter arrived.
says when the first part happened
We left before it started to rain.
We went for a meal after we had seen the film.
You can have some ice cream if you eat your dinner.
the first part may not happen

lesson.heading: only, like and than
lesson.text: **Only** says that something is not very big or not very much. **Like** makes a comparison. **Than** comes after a comparative adjective or adverb.

examples.text: He **only** sleeps for three hours every night.
I can swim better **than** they can!

lesson.heading: also, too and as well
lesson.text: **Also**, **too** and **as well** all say that something is extra. **Also** usually goes in the middle of the sentence; **too** and **as well** go at the end.

examples.text: He works in the shop and she works there **too**.
He works in the shop and she **also** works there.
He works in the shop and she works there **as well**.
I love swimming and my sister likes it very much **as well**.

lesson.text: These words are small but very important. Write a translation of each one in your notebook.

exercises.prompt: Blake liked school ___ he had many friends there.
exercises.explanation: Because explains why the first part happened.

exercises.prompt: Blake was seasick ___ he left the navy.
exercises.explanation: So introduces the result of the first part.

exercises.prompt: Blake left school ___ he joined the navy.
exercises.explanation: And adds extra information about what happened next.

exercises.prompt: He hadn't travelled much ___ he joined the navy.
exercises.explanation: Before shows that the first part happened first.

exercises.prompt: He will stay at the bank ___ he likes it there.
exercises.explanation: If says the first part will only happen when the second part happens.

exercises.prompt: He wants to get married ___ he's 30.
exercises.explanation: When says at what time the first part will happen.

exercises.prompt: Match each connecting word with its job in the sentence.
I love swimming and my brother loves swimming ___.
exercises.hint: (a short extra word at the end)
exercises.explanation: Too, as well and also all say that something is extra.

exercises.prompt: My brother and sister both swim, but I can swim better ___ they can!
exercises.explanation: Than comes after a comparative: better than, harder than.

exercises.prompt: Does the word join two parts of a sentence, or is it another connecting word?
Annabelle loved Aarav, and that is why she agreed to marry him. Say it.
exercises.answer: Annabelle agreed to marry Aarav because she loved him.

exercises.statement: They are rich but they aren't happy.
exercises.explanation: Correct. But shows a contrast between the two parts.

exercises.statement: We went home early so we were tired.
exercises.explanation: We went home early because we were tired. Because gives the reason, so gives the result.
